import type { NumberFormats } from './util';

export type Currency = {
  code: string;
  symbol: string;
  name: string;
  decimalPlaces: number;
  numberFormat: NumberFormats;
  symbolFirst: boolean;
};

// When adding a new currency with a higher decimal precision, make sure to update
// the MAX_SAFE_NUMBER in util.ts.
// When adding a currency, also update the translation map in
// packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/Currency.tsx for the translation.
// Number formats and symbol placement based on CLDR (Common Locale Data Repository) /
// LDML (Locale Data Markup Language) locale conventions and Intl.NumberFormat standards
// References:
// https://www.localeplanet.com/icu/decimal-symbols.html
// https://www.localeplanet.com/api/auto/currencymap.html
// prettier-ignore
export const currencies: Currency[] = [
  { code: '', name: 'None', symbol: '', decimalPlaces: 2, numberFormat: 'comma-dot', symbolFirst: true },
  { code: 'AED', name: 'UAE Dirham', symbol: 'د.إ', decimalPlaces: 2, numberFormat: 'comma-dot', symbolFirst: false },

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-14 22:52:32-0400)**_

Yes — it's already implemented, and it's more than just the settings panel. It's shipped behind an experimental feature flag.

**The wiring:**

1. **Currency data** — [currencies.ts](packages/loot-core/src/shared/currencies.ts) defines ~47 currencies with `symbol`, `decimalPlaces`, `numberFormat`, and `symbolFirst`, based on CLDR conventions.

2. **The settings UI you found** writes three synced prefs: `defaultCurrencyCode`, `currencySymbolPosition`, `currencySpaceBetweenAmountAndSymbol` (plus it derives `numberFormat` and `hideFraction` from the chosen currency).

3. **The actual formatting** lives in [useFormat.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts). `applyCurrencyStyling` ([useFormat.ts:140-164](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts#L140-L164)) reads those prefs and attaches the symbol — handling sign placement, the narrow no-break space (`\u202F`), and LTR isolation marks (`\u202A`/`\u202C`) so RTL symbols like `د.إ` don't scramble the digits. Decimal places also come from the currency ([useFormat.ts:179](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts#L179)).

4. **~87 files** in desktop-client consume `useFormat`, so most amounts across the app already render with the symbol.

5. **Formulas** have their own parallel path — [customFunctions.ts](packages/loot-core/src/shared/formulas/customFunctions.ts) reimplements the same styling for formula output, with per-call overrides.

**It's gated:** [settings/index.tsx:240](packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/index.tsx#L240) only renders `CurrencySettings` when `useFeatureFlag('currency')` is on, and [line 189-192](packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/index.tsx#L189-L192) actively resets `defaultCurrencyCode` to `''` if the flag is off. Enable it under Settings → Experimental ([Experimental.tsx:200](packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/Experimental.tsx#L200)). With no currency selected (code `''`), `applyCurrencyStyling` is skipped entirely — you get bare numbers, which is why it looks unimplemented by default.

**Where it's genuinely incomplete:** a number of components still call `integerToCurrency` directly instead of going through `useFormat` — [TransactionsTable.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/TransactionsTable.tsx), [budget/util.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/util.ts), [CloseAccountModal.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/CloseAccountModal.tsx), [BalanceHistoryGraph.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/BalanceHistoryGraph.tsx), the mobile transaction components, and others. That function only applies number formatting ([util.ts:447-456](packages/loot-core/src/shared/util.ts#L447-L456)) — no symbol. So those spots will show unstyled amounts even with a currency selected. `useFormat` itself notes this in a comment at [lines 132-135](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts#L132-L135): the intent is to migrate everything off the global formatter onto the reactive hook.

So if you were planning to build currency formatting, the better framing is finishing the migration rather than starting fresh.

Here's the scope, split by what's actually independent.

## The dropdown itself: small

Adding a Currency dropdown alongside Numbers / Dates / First day of the week is genuinely cheap. [Format.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/Format.tsx) already has the exact pattern — three `<Column>` wrappers around `<Select>`. `CurrencySettings` is structurally the same thing in its own `<Setting>` card, so it's either a move into `FormatSettings` as a fourth `<Column>`, or leave it as its own card and just ungate it.

One design snag: [Currency.tsx:105-114](packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/Currency.tsx#L105-L114) has the currency dropdown *overwrite* `numberFormat` and `hideFraction`. If it sits in the same card as those controls, picking a currency visibly rewrites the two dropdowns next to it. Fine, but you'd want it deliberate.

**~1-2 files.**

## Ungating: small, but it's the part that exposes everything else

- [useFeatureFlag.ts:10](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFeatureFlag.ts#L10) — `currency: false` → `true`, or drop the flag
- [settings/index.tsx:189-192](packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/index.tsx#L189-L192) — delete the effect that force-resets `defaultCurrencyCode` to `''`
- [Experimental.tsx:200](packages/desktop-client/src/components/settings/Experimental.tsx#L200) and [prefs.ts:6](packages/loot-core/src/types/prefs.ts#L6) — remove the flag entry

**~4 files.** Low risk on its own, because the default currency stays `''` and `''` means "no symbol" — existing users see no change until they opt in.

## The migration: this is the real work

**13 files, ~30 call sites**, in two categories that need opposite treatment.

**Display sites that should gain the symbol (~13 calls, 7 files):** [CategoryAutocomplete.tsx:458,466](packages/desktop-client/src/components/autocomplete/CategoryAutocomplete.tsx#L458), [CloseAccountModal.tsx:174](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/CloseAccountModal.tsx#L174), [TransactionsTable.tsx:1845,1943,2050](packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/TransactionsTable.tsx#L1845), [BalanceHistoryGraph.tsx:318](packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/BalanceHistoryGraph.tsx#L318), [TransactionEdit.tsx:301,313,2204](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/TransactionEdit.tsx#L301), [TransactionListItem.tsx:293,308](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/TransactionListItem.tsx#L293), [TransactionList.tsx:505](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/TransactionList.tsx#L505). These are mechanical — swap to `format(value, 'financial')`.

**Edit/serialization sites that must *not* gain a symbol (~17 calls, 6 files):** all the `amountToCurrency` uses in [ImportTransactionsModal/Transaction.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/ImportTransactionsModal/Transaction.tsx), [CalculatorAmountInput.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/CalculatorAmountInput.tsx), [FocusableAmountInput.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/FocusableAmountInput.tsx), the four input-value calls in TransactionsTable, plus [table/utils.ts:64-65](packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/table/utils.ts#L64-L65) and [CoverMenu.tsx:56](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/envelope/CoverMenu.tsx#L56). These want `forEdit`/`fromEdit`, which already exist on the hook. [budget/util.ts:81](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/util.ts#L81) is a third thing entirely — it round-trips through a string purely to get a number for a color decision, and a symbol would break `currencyToAmount`; that one should probably just stop calling the formatter.

**The structural blocker:** `table/utils.ts` and `budget/util.ts` are plain modules, not components, so they can't call a hook. `useFormat` handles this today with an acknowledged hack — [lines 132-138](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts#L132-L138) push the number format into a module-level global via `setNumberFormat`. There's no equivalent global for currency (I checked — no `setCurrency` in shared). So you either thread `format` down as a parameter, or add a parallel global. That's the one design decision in this whole thing, and it's worth making before touching the 13 files.

Good news: **the entire reports directory is already clean** — every reports file that formats money goes through `useFormat`. Charts, tooltips, cards, all fine.

## The thing that makes this more than cosmetic

`integerToCurrency` defaults to `decimalPlaces = 2` ([util.ts:447-456](packages/loot-core/src/shared/util.ts#L447-L456)). For JPY, KRW, and IRR — 0-decimal currencies in [currencies.ts](packages/loot-core/src/shared/currencies.ts) — amounts are stored via `amountToInteger(value, 0)`, so ¥1000 is the integer `1000`. Every one of these bypass sites divides by 100 and renders **¥10.00**. That's a wrong number, not just a missing symbol. It's the strongest reason the flag can't come off before the migration lands, and the best framing for the PR.

## Tests

`settings.test.ts` and `settings.mobile.test.ts` VRT snapshots change the moment the card becomes visible by default — [settings.test.ts-snapshots](packages/desktop-client/e2e/settings.test.ts-snapshots/) has 3 images, mobile has 6. Regenerate via `yarn vrt:docker`. Transaction-table and mobile-transaction snapshots should be unaffected as long as the default stays `''`, but that's worth confirming rather than assuming.

## Rough shape

I'd do it as three PRs rather than one: **(1)** migrate the 13 display sites, **(2)** migrate the edit sites and resolve the non-hook question, **(3)** ungate + move the dropdown into Format + regenerate VRT. PR 3 is an afternoon; PRs 1 and 2 are the substance, with PR 2 carrying the only real design risk.

Want me to start on the display-site migration, or work up the non-hook approach first since it constrains everything downstream?

`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts`

```ts
export type FormatType =
  | 'string' | 'number' | 'percentage'
  | 'financial' | 'financial-with-sign' | 'financial-no-decimals';

export type UseFormatResult = {
  (value: unknown, type?: FormatType): string;   // default type is 'string'
  forEdit: (value: IntegerAmount) => string;
  fromEdit: (value: string, defaultValue?: number | null) => IntegerAmount | null;
  currency: Currency;
};

export function useFormat(): UseFormatResult
```

Key behaviors relevant to the migration:
- Import alias in current code is `#hooks/useFormat` (post subpath-import migration, e.g. `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/spreadsheet/CellValue.tsx:9`).
- For `'financial'`, it accepts `number | null | undefined | ''` (null/empty coerced to 0) and also strings (legacy path, `useFormat.ts:70-88` — throws on non-numeric strings). So `format(x ?? 0, 'financial')` is the direct replacement for `integerToCurrency(x || 0)`.
- Currency styling is applied only when `activeCurrency.code !== ''` (`useFormat.ts:196`), and it wraps the symbol in Unicode bidi isolates: `\u202A<symbol>\u202C` plus optional `\u202F` narrow no-break space (`useFormat.ts:153-159`). This matters for anything that string-interpolates the output (see TransactionList finding below).
- It calls 5 `useSyncedPref` hooks internally, so it must be called at React-component top level.

## `FinancialText` / `CellValue`

- `FinancialText`: `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/FinancialText.tsx` — pure presentational, applies `styles.tnum` (tabular numerals). It does **not** format; it's orthogonal to `useFormat`. It takes `as` to swap the element.

Only useful for **spreadsheet-bound** values (`Binding<SheetName, FieldName>`). None of the 13 sites are spreadsheet bindings, so `CellValue` is not applicable. `CellValueText:83` is the canonical "format + FinancialText + PrivacyFilter" combination to mirror.

function Footer({
  transactions,
  isAdding,
  onAdd,
  onSave,
  onSplit,
  onAddSplit,
  onEmptySplitFound,
  editingField,
  onEditField,
}: FooterProps) {
  const [transaction, ...childTransactions] = transactions;
  const emptySplitTransaction = childTransactions.find(t => t.amount === 0);
  const onClickRemainingSplit = () => {
    if (childTransactions.length === 0) {
      onSplit(transaction.id);
    } else {
      if (!emptySplitTransaction) {
        onAddSplit(transaction.id);
      } else {
        onEmptySplitFound?.(emptySplitTransaction.id);

```text
import { evalArithmetic } from '@actual-app/core/shared/arithmetic';
import { currentDay } from '@actual-app/core/shared/months';
import {
  amountToInteger,
  integerToCurrencyWithDecimal,
} from '@actual-app/core/shared/util';
import type { CurrencyAmount } from '@actual-app/core/shared/util';
import type {
  AccountEntity,
  CategoryEntity,
  TransactionEntity,
} from '@actual-app/core/types/models';
import { isValid as isDateValid, parseISO } from 'date-fns';

export type SerializedTransaction = Omit<TransactionEntity, 'date'> & {
  date: string;
  debit: CurrencyAmount;
  credit: CurrencyAmount;
};

export type TransactionEditFunction = (
  id: TransactionEntity['id'],
  name: string,
) => void;

export type TransactionUpdateFunction = <T extends keyof SerializedTransaction>(
  name: T,
  value: SerializedTransaction[T],
) => void;

export function serializeTransaction(
  transaction: TransactionEntity,
  showZeroInDeposit?: boolean,
): SerializedTransaction {
  const { amount, date: originalDate } = transaction;

  let debit = amount < 0 ? -amount : null;
  let credit = amount > 0 ? amount : null;

  if (amount === 0) {
    if (showZeroInDeposit) {
      credit = 0;
    } else {
      debit = 0;
    }
  }

  let date = originalDate;
  // Validate the date format
  if (!isDateValid(parseISO(date))) {
    // Be a little forgiving if the date isn't valid. This at least
    // stops the UI from crashing, but this is a serious problem with
    // the data. This allows the user to go through and see empty
    // dates and manually fix them.
    console.error(`Date '${date}' is not valid.`);
    // TODO: the fact that the date type is not nullable but we are setting it to null needs to be changed
    date = null as unknown as string;
  }

  // Convert with decimals here so the value doesn't lose decimals and formatter will show or hide them.
  return {
    ...transaction,
    date,
    debit: debit != null ? integerToCurrencyWithDecimal(debit) : '',
    credit: credit != null ? integerToCurrencyWithDecimal(credit) : '',
  };
}

export function deserializeTransaction(
  transaction: SerializedTransaction,
  originalTransaction: TransactionEntity,
) {
  const { debit, credit, date: originalDate, ...realTransaction } = transaction;

  let amount: number | null;
  if (debit !== '') {
    const parsed = evalArithmetic(debit, null);
    amount = parsed != null ? -parsed : null;
  } else {
    amount = evalArithmetic(credit, null);
  }

  amount =
    amount != null ? amountToInteger(amount) : originalTransaction.amount;
  let date = originalDate;
  if (date == null) {
    date = originalTransaction.date || currentDay();
  }

  return { ...realTransaction, date, amount };
}

export function isLastChild(
  transactions: readonly TransactionEntity[],
  index: number,
) {
  const trans = transactions[index];
  return (
    trans &&
    trans.is_child &&
    (transactions[index + 1] == null ||
      transactions[index + 1].parent_id !== trans.parent_id)
  );
}

export function selectAscDesc(
  field: string,
  ascDesc: 'asc' | 'desc',
  clicked: string,
  defaultAscDesc: 'asc' | 'desc' = 'asc',
) {
  return field === clicked
    ? ascDesc === 'asc'
      ? 'desc'
      : 'asc'
    : defaultAscDesc;
}

// Decides whether a rule result should be applied to a field while the user is
// entering a new transaction. By default rules only fill fields the user left
// empty, so their manual input isn't overwritten. The exception is the notes
// field: append/prepend notes rules intentionally preserve the existing note and
// add text before or after it, so we allow those through. The check stays
// idempotent — rules are re-run on every keystroke during entry, so we must not
// re-add text that the previous run already applied.
export function shouldApplyRuleChange(
  field: string,
  currentValue: unknown,
  nextValue: unknown,
) {
  if (
    currentValue == null ||
    currentValue === '' ||
    currentValue === 0 ||
    currentValue === false
  ) {
    return true;
  }

  if (
    field !== 'notes' ||
    typeof currentValue !== 'string' ||
    typeof nextValue !== 'string' ||
    nextValue === currentValue
  ) {
    return false;
  }

  // The rule preserved the user's note only if the result still contains it
  // verbatim. Otherwise treat it as an overwrite and keep the manual note.
  const index = nextValue.indexOf(currentValue);
  if (index === -1) {
    return false;
  }

  const prepended = nextValue.slice(0, index);
  const appended = nextValue.slice(index + currentValue.length);

  // If the note already starts/ends with these exact additions, a previous rule
  // run already applied them — applying again would duplicate the text.
  const alreadyApplied =
    (prepended === '' || currentValue.startsWith(prepended)) &&
    (appended === '' || currentValue.endsWith(appended));

  return !alreadyApplied;
}

export function makeTemporaryTransactions(
  currentAccountId: AccountEntity['id'] | null | undefined,
  currentCategoryId: CategoryEntity['id'] | null | undefined,
  lastDate?: string | null,
): TransactionEntity[] {
  return [
    {
      id: 'temp',
      date: lastDate || currentDay(),
      // TODO: consider making this default to an empty string
      account: (currentAccountId || null) as string,
      category: currentCategoryId || undefined,
      cleared: false,
      // TODO: either make this nullable or find a way to make this not null
      amount: null as unknown as number,
    },
  ];
}

## `useFormat` — exact signature and return shape

`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts`

```ts
export type FormatType =
  | 'string' | 'number' | 'percentage'
  | 'financial' | 'financial-with-sign' | 'financial-no-decimals';

export type UseFormatResult = {
  (value: unknown, type?: FormatType): string;   // default type is 'string'
  forEdit: (value: IntegerAmount) => string;
  fromEdit: (value: string, defaultValue?: number | null) => IntegerAmount | null;
  currency: Currency;
};

export function useFormat(): UseFormatResult
```

Key behaviors relevant to the migration:
- Import alias in current code is `#hooks/useFormat` (post subpath-import migration, e.g. `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/spreadsheet/CellValue.tsx:9`).
- For `'financial'`, it accepts `number | null | undefined | ''` (null/empty coerced to 0) and also strings (legacy path, `useFormat.ts:70-88` — throws on non-numeric strings). So `format(x ?? 0, 'financial')` is the direct replacement for `integerToCurrency(x || 0)`.
- Currency styling is applied only when `activeCurrency.code !== ''` (`useFormat.ts:196`), and it wraps the symbol in Unicode bidi isolates: `\u202A<symbol>\u202C` plus optional `\u202F` narrow no-break space (`useFormat.ts:153-159`). This matters for anything that string-interpolates the output (see TransactionList finding below).
- It calls 5 `useSyncedPref` hooks internally, so it must be called at React-component top level.

## `FinancialText` / `CellValue`

- `FinancialText`: `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/FinancialText.tsx` — pure presentational, applies `styles.tnum` (tabular numerals). It does **not** format; it's orthogonal to `useFormat`. It takes `as` to swap the element.
- `CellValue` / `CellValueText`: `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/spreadsheet/CellValue.tsx:37` and `:72`. Only useful for **spreadsheet-bound** values (`Binding<SheetName, FieldName>`). None of the 13 sites are spreadsheet bindings, so `CellValue` is not applicable. `CellValueText:83` is the canonical "format + FinancialText + PrivacyFilter" combination to mirror.
- `Cell` in `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/table.tsx:749` already calls `useFormat()` and threads a `formatter` prop (`table.tsx:761-762`), but only via `SheetCell`; the plain `Cell` at TransactionsTable:1838 gets a pre-formatted string `value`.

## Background

Actual has an experimental `currency` feature flag (default false, packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFeatureFlag.ts:10). When enabled, users pick a default currency in Settings, which sets synced prefs `defaultCurrencyCode`, `currencySymbolPosition`, `currencySpaceBetweenAmountAndSymbol`.

The hook `useFormat()` at packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts is the correct funnel: it applies the currency symbol (with bidi isolates ‪/‬ and optional   narrow no-break space) AND per-currency decimal places. Its signature:

```ts
type UseFormatResult = {
  (value: unknown, type?: FormatType): string;
  forEdit: (value: IntegerAmount) => string;
  fromEdit: (value: string, defaultValue?: number|null) => IntegerAmount | null;
  currency: Currency;
};
// FormatType = 'string'|'number'|'percentage'|'financial'|'financial-with-sign'|'financial-no-decimals'
```

The global `integerToCurrency(integerAmount, formatter?, decimalPlaces = 2)` in packages/loot-core/src/shared/util.ts:447 hardcodes 2 decimal places and never adds a symbol. For 0-decimal currencies (JPY, KRW, IRR) this renders a WRONG NUMBER (¥1000 stored as integer 1000 renders as "10.00"), not just a missing symbol.

~87 files already use useFormat; the whole reports/ directory is already clean. These 13 are display-path stragglers.

export function toRelaxedNumber(currencyAmount: CurrencyAmount): Amount {
  return integerToAmount(currencyToInteger(currencyAmount) || 0);
}

export function integerToCurrency(
  integerAmount: IntegerAmount,
  formatter = getNumberFormat().formatter,
  decimalPlaces: number = 2,
) {
  const divisor = Math.pow(10, decimalPlaces);
  const amount = safeNumber(integerAmount) / divisor;

  return formatter.format(amount);
}

export function integerToCurrencyWithDecimal(
  integerAmount: IntegerAmount,
  currencyCode?: string,
) {
  if (currencyCode !== undefined) {
    const dp = getDecimalPlaces(currencyCode);
    return integerToCurrency(
      integerAmount,
      getNumberFormat({ ...numberFormatConfig, decimalPlaces: dp }).formatter,
      dp,
    );
  }

import React, { forwardRef } from 'react';
import type { HTMLProps, ReactNode, Ref } from 'react';

import { css, cx } from '@emotion/css';

import type { CSSProperties } from './styles';

type TextProps = Omit<HTMLProps<HTMLSpanElement>, 'style'> & {
  innerRef?: Ref<HTMLSpanElement>;
  className?: string;
  children?: ReactNode;
  style?: CSSProperties;
};

export const Text = forwardRef<HTMLSpanElement, TextProps>((props, ref) => {
  const { className = '', style, innerRef, ...restProps } = props;
  return (
    <span
      {...restProps}
      ref={innerRef ?? ref}
      className={cx(className, css(style))}
    />
  );
});

**Sites 11-12 (TransactionListItem) manually spread `...styles.tnum`, which is exactly what the `FinancialText` component does. Should this PR also switch those to `<FinancialText>`?**

Options:
- **Pure format() swap only (Recommended)** - Keep the PR to one mechanical change: integerToCurrency → format(x, 'financial'). FinancialText adoption becomes a separate follow-up. Easiest to review, smallest diff, no DOM changes so VRT snapshots stay untouched.
- **Also adopt FinancialText** - Migrate sites 11-12 (and optionally 3 and 7) to <FinancialText> in the same PR. Fewer total PRs and aligns with the AGENTS.md typography convention, but changes rendered DOM and may require regenerating VRT snapshots.

**Site 13 (TransactionList.tsx:505) sits in a `case 'amount':` branch whose menu item is currently commented out — it's dead code. Its formatted value also gets used as a markdown link target and an object key, where a currency symbol and bidi control chars could corrupt it. What should happen to it?**

Options:
- **Migrate it anyway (Recommended)** - Swap it like the others so the branch is correct if it's ever re-enabled, and note the markdown/bidi risk in the PR description for the reviewer. Keeps the migration complete — no straggler left calling the old util.
- **Skip it, leave a comment** - Leave the call as-is with a TODO explaining it needs the bidi/markdown question resolved before migrating. Avoids shipping an unverifiable change, but leaves one integerToCurrency straggler.
- **Delete the dead branch** - Remove the unreachable `case 'amount':` entirely along with the commented-out menu item. Cleanest result, but it's unrelated cleanup that widens the PR beyond the migration.


**Answer:** Pure format() swap only (Recommended), Migrate it anyway (Recommended)

let numberFormatConfig: {
  format: NumberFormats;
  hideFraction: boolean;
} = {
  format: 'comma-dot',
  hideFraction: false,
};

export function parseNumberFormat({
  format,
  hideFraction,
}: {
  format?: string;
  hideFraction?: string | boolean;
}) {
  return {
    format: isNumberFormat(format) ? format : 'comma-dot',
    hideFraction: String(hideFraction) === 'true',
  };
}

export function setNumberFormat(config: typeof numberFormatConfig) {
  numberFormatConfig = config;
}

export function getNumberFormat({
  format = numberFormatConfig.format,
  hideFraction = numberFormatConfig.hideFraction,
  decimalPlaces,
}: {
  format?: NumberFormats;
  hideFraction?: boolean;
  decimalPlaces?: number;
} = numberFormatConfig) {
  let locale, thousandsSeparator, decimalSeparator;

  const currentFormat = format || numberFormatConfig.format;
  const currentHideFraction =
    typeof hideFraction === 'boolean'
      ? hideFraction
      : numberFormatConfig.hideFraction;

  switch (format) {
    case 'space-comma':
      locale = 'fr-FR';
      thousandsSeparator = '\u202F';
      decimalSeparator = ',';
      break;
    case 'dot-comma':
      locale = 'de-DE';
      thousandsSeparator = '.';
```

function Footer({
  transactions,
  isAdding,
  onAdd,
  onSave,
  onSplit,
  onAddSplit,
  onEmptySplitFound,
  editingField,
  onEditField,
}: FooterProps) {
  const [transaction, ...childTransactions] = transactions;
  const emptySplitTransaction = childTransactions.find(t => t.amount === 0);

    if (childTransactions.length === 0) {

expect.extend({
  payeesToHaveFavoriteStars(
    container: Element[],
    validPayeeListWithFavorite: string[],
  ) {
    const incorrectStarList: string[] = [];
    const foundStarList: string[] = [];
    validPayeeListWithFavorite.forEach(payeeItem => {
      const shouldHaveFavorite = payeeItem != null;
      let found = false;
      if (container[0].querySelectorAll('svg').length === 1) {
        found = true;
        foundStarList.push(payeeItem);
      }
      if (shouldHaveFavorite !== found) {
        incorrectStarList.push(payeeItem);
      }
    });
    if (
      foundStarList.length !== validPayeeListWithFavorite.length ||
      incorrectStarList.length > 0
    ) {
      return {
        message: () =>
          `Expected ${validPayeeListWithFavorite.join(
            ', ',
          )} to have favorite stars.` +
          `Received ${
            foundStarList.length
          } items with favorite stars. Incorrect: ${incorrectStarList.join(
            ', ',
          )}`,
        pass: false,
      };
    } else {
      return {
        message: () =>
          `Expected ${String(
            validPayeeListWithFavorite,
          )} to have favorite stars`,
        pass: true,
      };
    }
  },
});

function expectToBeEditingField(
  container: HTMLElement,
  name: string,
  rowIndex: number,
  isNew?: boolean,
) {
  let field: Element;
  if (isNew) {
    field = queryNewField(container, name, '', rowIndex);
  } else {
    field = queryField(container, name, '', rowIndex);
  }
  const input: HTMLInputElement = field.querySelector(':focus')!;
  expect(input).toBeTruthy();
  expect(container.ownerDocument.activeElement).toBe(input);
  return input;
}

104:- Add a release note. These notes get used when generating the full release note at the next release.
105-- Once your PR is ready for maintainers to review, remove the `[WIP]` label from the PR title.
106-- Sometimes it can take some time for the maintainers to review your PR for approval. Please keep your PR up to date with the current master branch by merging or rebasing until your PR gets merged.
107-
108:### Writing Good Release Notes
109-
110:Before creating your pull request, run the command `yarn generate:release-notes`. This will guide you through the steps necessary for creating a release note for your change. You will be asked the following questions:
111-
112-1. Comma-separated GitHub username(s) - your GitHub username, or if multiple people are involved, you can specify them all (e.g. `username1, username2`)
113-2. Filename slug - a short descriptive slug used as `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`. Auto-filled from your branch name (or PR title if one is detected).
114:3. Release Note Type - this will give you a select field with 4 options from the "Valid categories" section below
115-4. Brief Summary - this is a short summary of your changes.
116-
117:For a better experience with the release note generation script, consider installing [the official GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli) and running `gh auth login`. This will allow the script to automatically fill in some information like your GitHub username and current PR information if you've already opened one from a fork you created.
118-
119-Create a Markdown file in the upcoming-release-notes directory of the repository you're contributing to. Pick a short, descriptive filename (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`); the PR link in the published changelog is resolved automatically when the release is generated, so you don't need to know the PR number. Numeric filenames like `1234.md` also remain valid. The file should contain front matter with a category key (defining which header to put the entry under) and an authors key (defining the author of the entry). The body of the file should contain the changelog entry. Keep it short and clear — ideally one sentence, and also non-technical (unless the category is "Maintenance"). Copy-paste the template below to get started!
120-
121-```markdown
122----
123-category: Features
124-authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
125----
126-
127-Add option to include exchange rate multiplier during import
128-```
129-
130-Valid categories:
131-
132-- `Features`: New features
133-- `Enhancements`: Improvements to existing features
134-- `Bugfix`: Bug fixes
135-- `Maintenance`: Internal changes that don't directly affect users
136-
137-The `authors` key should be an array with the GitHub usernames of the people who contributed to the PR. In most cases, this should just be you but you can add multiple people if needed.
138-
139-Try to phrase your message as a command, e.g. "Add option to include exchange rate multiplier during import" rather than "Added option to include exchange rate multiplier during import" or "Adds option to include exchange rate multiplier during import." Generally your message should match the PR title, but you can change it if you think it's more clear.
140-
141-### The Design Strategy Of Actual
142-
143-The goal of the UI is to be minimalistic, but expose more advanced features progressively as the user interacts with the product (for example: the notes button is not visible by default if an account has no notes, but it becomes persistent visible if there are notes). We advocate for a similar approach in other places too. We are against adding a button/user setting for every little piece of UI (sizes, paddings, margins, etc.) as that goes against this simple design philosophy.
144-
145-The settings screen needs to also remain a place where core settings lives, we don't really want to have a myriad of options in here for each and every setting within the UI, doing that makes the code un-manageable for future contributors and clutters up and confuses things for the users of Actual Budget.
146-

```text
import { useCallback } from 'react';

import type { SyncedPrefs } from '@actual-app/core/types/prefs';

import { saveSyncedPrefs } from '#prefs/prefsSlice';
import { useDispatch, useSelector } from '#redux';

type SetSyncedPrefAction<K extends keyof SyncedPrefs> = (
  value: SyncedPrefs[K],
) => void;

export function useSyncedPref<K extends keyof SyncedPrefs>(
  prefName: K,
): [SyncedPrefs[K], SetSyncedPrefAction<K>] {
  const dispatch = useDispatch();
  const setPref = useCallback<SetSyncedPrefAction<K>>(
    value => {
      void dispatch(
        saveSyncedPrefs({
          prefs: { [prefName]: value },
        }),
      );
    },
    [prefName, dispatch],
  );
  const pref = useSelector(state => state.prefs.synced[prefName]);

  return [pref, setPref];
}
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
import type { FeatureFlag } from '@actual-app/core/types/prefs';

import { useSyncedPref } from './useSyncedPref';

const DEFAULT_FEATURE_FLAG_STATE: Record<FeatureFlag, boolean> = {
  goalTemplatesEnabled: false,
  goalTemplatesUIEnabled: false,
  actionTemplating: false,
  formulaMode: false,
  currency: false,
  ageOfMoneyReport: false,
  balanceForecastReport: false,
  customThemes: false,
  budgetAnalysisReport: false,
  payeeLocations: false,
  enableBanking: false,
  sankeyReport: false,
  akahuBankSync: false,
  mobileCalculator: false,
};

export function useFeatureFlag(name: FeatureFlag): boolean {
  const [value] = useSyncedPref(`flags.${name}`);

  return value === undefined
    ? DEFAULT_FEATURE_FLAG_STATE[name] || false
    : String(value) === 'true';
}
```
</details></tool-use>

104:- Add a release note. These notes get used when generating the full release note at the next release.
105-- Once your PR is ready for maintainers to review, remove the `[WIP]` label from the PR title.
106-- Sometimes it can take some time for the maintainers to review your PR for approval. Please keep your PR up to date with the current master branch by merging or rebasing until your PR gets merged.
107-
108:### Writing Good Release Notes
109-
110:Before creating your pull request, run the command `yarn generate:release-notes`. This will guide you through the steps necessary for creating a release note for your change. You will be asked the following questions:
111-
112-1. Comma-separated GitHub username(s) - your GitHub username, or if multiple people are involved, you can specify them all (e.g. `username1, username2`)
113-2. Filename slug - a short descriptive slug used as `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`. Auto-filled from your branch name (or PR title if one is detected).
114:3. Release Note Type - this will give you a select field with 4 options from the "Valid categories" section below
115-4. Brief Summary - this is a short summary of your changes.
116-
117:For a better experience with the release note generation script, consider installing [the official GitHub CLI](https://github.com/cli/cli) and running `gh auth login`. This will allow the script to automatically fill in some information like your GitHub username and current PR information if you've already opened one from a fork you created.
118-
119-Create a Markdown file in the upcoming-release-notes directory of the repository you're contributing to. Pick a short, descriptive filename (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`); the PR link in the published changelog is resolved automatically when the release is generated, so you don't need to know the PR number. Numeric filenames like `1234.md` also remain valid. The file should contain front matter with a category key (defining which header to put the entry under) and an authors key (defining the author of the entry). The body of the file should contain the changelog entry. Keep it short and clear — ideally one sentence, and also non-technical (unless the category is "Maintenance"). Copy-paste the template below to get started!
120-
121-```markdown
122----
123-category: Features
124-authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
125----
126-
127-Add option to include exchange rate multiplier during import
128-```
129-
130-Valid categories:
131-
132-- `Features`: New features
133-- `Enhancements`: Improvements to existing features
134-- `Bugfix`: Bug fixes
135-- `Maintenance`: Internal changes that don't directly affect users
136-
137-The `authors` key should be an array with the GitHub usernames of the people who contributed to the PR. In most cases, this should just be you but you can add multiple people if needed.
138-
139-Try to phrase your message as a command, e.g. "Add option to include exchange rate multiplier during import" rather than "Added option to include exchange rate multiplier during import" or "Adds option to include exchange rate multiplier during import." Generally your message should match the PR title, but you can change it if you think it's more clear.
140-

142-

# Migrate 13 currency display sites to `useFormat`

## Context

Actual has an experimental `currency` feature flag (default `false`,
[useFeatureFlag.ts:10](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFeatureFlag.ts#L10), tracking issue
[#5191](https://github.com/actualbudget/actual/issues/5191)). When enabled, the user picks a default
currency in Settings and the app is supposed to render amounts with that currency's symbol and
decimal precision.

[`useFormat()`](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts) is the funnel that does this — it
applies the symbol (with bidi isolates and optional narrow no-break space) and the per-currency
decimal places. ~87 files already go through it, and the whole `reports/` directory is clean.

But 13 display sites across 7 files still call the global
[`integerToCurrency`](packages/loot-core/src/shared/util.ts#L447-L456), which never adds a symbol
**and hardcodes `decimalPlaces = 2`**. For the 0-decimal currencies in
[currencies.ts](packages/loot-core/src/shared/currencies.ts) — JPY, KRW, IRR — amounts are stored as
`amountToInteger(value, 0)`, so ¥1000 is the integer `1000` and these sites render **¥10.00**. That
is a wrong number, not just a missing symbol, and it's the reason the flag can't be turned on until
this is done.

This is the first of three PRs. It covers **display sites only**. Edit/serialization paths
([table/utils.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/table/utils.ts),
[budget/util.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/util.ts),
[CoverMenu.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/envelope/CoverMenu.tsx), the
`amountToCurrency` input sites) must **not** gain a symbol and are explicitly out of scope — they
need `forEdit`/`fromEdit` and a solution for non-hook module contexts, which is PR 2. Flipping the
flag and moving the dropdown into Format settings is PR 3.

### Scope decisions (confirmed)

- **Pure `format()` swap only.** No `<FinancialText>` adoption in this PR, even where sites manually
  spread `...styles.tnum`. Keeps the diff mechanical and leaves rendered DOM unchanged, so VRT
  snapshots stay untouched. `FinancialText` is an AGENTS.md convention, not lint-enforced
  (`actual/typography` only catches curly quotes), so deferring is safe.
- **Site 13 gets migrated** despite being dead code, so no straggler is left on the old util. The
  markdown/bidi risk gets called out in the PR description for the reviewer.

## The pattern

Applied identically at every site:

```diff
-import { integerToCurrency } from '@actual-app/core/shared/util';
+import { useFormat } from '#hooks/useFormat';

 export function SomeComponent() {
+  const format = useFormat();
   ...
-  {integerToCurrency(amount)}
+  {format(amount, 'financial')}
```

Conventions, both unanimous in the codebase:

- `const format = useFormat()` — 91 of 91 existing call sites.
- `import { format as formatDate } from 'date-fns'` — the alias used in all 15 files that need both.

Drop the `integerToCurrency` import once a file's last use is gone; several files import it
alongside other utils, so trim the named import rather than deleting the line.

## Per-file changes

### 1. [CategoryAutocomplete.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/autocomplete/CategoryAutocomplete.tsx) — 2 sites

Component `CategoryItem` (~line 379). Lines ~458 and ~466, already inside `<FinancialText>`.
`integerToCurrency(toBudget || 0)` → `format(toBudget || 0, 'financial')`, same for `balance`.
Cleanest of the seven — no collisions, no i18n.

### 2. [CloseAccountModal.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/CloseAccountModal.tsx) — 1 site

Component `CloseAccountModal` (~line 48); add the hook beside `useTranslation()` at ~line 53. Line
~174 is inside a `<Trans>` as `{{ balance: ... } as TransObjectLiteral}`. Calling `format()` inline
inside the object literal is fine — that's the established pattern in
[BalanceWithCarryover.tsx:165-212](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/BalanceWithCarryover.tsx#L165-L212).
File is `// @ts-strict-ignore`; leave that alone.

### 3. [TransactionsTable.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/TransactionsTable.tsx) — 3 sites

Two components, two separate `const format = useFormat()` declarations:

- `Transaction` memo (~line 914) covers line ~1845 (read-only balance `<Cell>`) and ~1943
  (DragPreview).
- `TransactionError` (~line 2026) covers line ~2050. Its body is a `switch` with early returns —
  **put the hook on the first line of the function body, above the switch**, or it becomes a
  conditional hook.

**Preserve the empty branch at ~1845.** The expression is
`runningBalance == null || isChild || isTemporaryId(id) ? '' : integerToCurrency(runningBalance)`.
Only the second branch changes; `format('', 'financial')` returns `"0.00"`, not `""`
([useFormat.ts:70-71](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts#L70-L71)).

Do **not** touch the `debit`/`credit` `InputCell`s at ~1783 and ~1820 or their `amountToCurrency`
calls — those are the edit path, fed by `serializeTransaction` and parsed back by
`deserializeTransaction`.

The file already aliases date-fns as `format as formatDate` (line 78), so `format` is free.

### 4. [BalanceHistoryGraph.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/BalanceHistoryGraph.tsx) — 1 site

Component `BalanceHistoryGraph` (~line 30). Line ~318, hover tooltip, already inside
`<PrivacyFilter>`.

**Name collision — the only one.** Line 12 is
`import { eachMonthOfInterval, format, subMonths } from 'date-fns';` and `format` is used at line
133. Alias it to `formatDate` and update line 133, matching the convention in the other 15 files.

### 5. [TransactionEdit.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/TransactionEdit.tsx) — 3 sites

Two components, both currently hook-free — this adds their first hook:

- `Footer` (~line 245) covers lines ~301 and ~313, both `<Trans>` interpolations using bare
  `{{ amount: ... }}` with no `TransObjectLiteral` cast. Both expressions are identical; hoist to a
  single `const amountLeft = format(...)` above the `return`.
- `FillRemainingButton` (~line 2180) covers line ~2204, also a `<Trans>`.

Both still return `string`, so the existing i18n typing should hold without adding casts.

### 6. [TransactionListItem.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/TransactionListItem.tsx) — 2 sites

Component `TransactionListItem` (~line 80), already hook-heavy. Lines ~293 (row amount) and ~308
(running balance). Leave the manual `...styles.tnum` spreads at ~283 and ~299 exactly as they are.

### 7. [TransactionList.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/TransactionList.tsx) — 1 site

Component `SelectedTransactionsFloatingActionBar` (~line 277). Line ~505 sits in an `onSuccess`
callback — declare the hook at component top and reference it through the closure.

Call out in the PR description: `displayValue` flows into a markdown link label *and* a `#` link
target at ~line 516, and is used as an object key in `messageActions` at ~518. Once a symbol and
`‪`/`‬`/` ` are present, those are no longer plain digits. The branch is currently
unreachable (the `'amount'` menu item is commented out), so nothing breaks today, but a reviewer
should know before it's re-enabled.

## Watch-outs

- **Conditional hooks.** `TransactionError` (switch with early returns) and the render-callback
  sites in `BalanceHistoryGraph` / `TransactionList` — the hook goes at component top level, never
  inside the callback or after a return.
- **The `''` branch** at TransactionsTable ~1845.
- **`hideFraction` is not a conflict.** `Transaction` takes a `hideFraction` prop, but it's only used
  for `letterSpacing` at line 1191 — never for number formatting. `useFormat` reads the pref itself.
  No divergence.
- **Don't widen into edit paths.** If a call site's output is later passed to `currencyToAmount`,
  `evalArithmetic`, or an input `value`, it belongs to PR 2.

## Tests

No new tests needed; this is a behavior-preserving swap at the default currency.

- **Unit:** only [TransactionsTable.test.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/TransactionsTable.test.tsx)
  touches these components, and its `integerToCurrency` assertions at lines 523 and 531 target the
  `debit`/`credit` cells — the edit path, untouched. They should pass unchanged.
- **VRT:** snapshots exist for `transactions`, `transactions.mobile`, `accounts`, `accounts.mobile`.
  With no currency selected, `getCurrency('')` gives `decimalPlaces: 2` and an empty symbol, so
  `format(x, 'financial')` is byte-identical to `integerToCurrency(x)` and
  [useFormat.ts:196](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts#L196) skips styling entirely.
  **Expect zero snapshot changes — if any snapshot moves, that's a real regression, not a rebaseline.**

Run:

```bash
yarn typecheck
yarn lint:fix
yarn workspace @actual-app/web run vitest --run TransactionsTable
yarn test
```

## Verification

The unit tests prove nothing about the actual fix, since they run at the default currency. Prove it
manually:

1. `yarn start`, then **View demo** on the setup screen (after "Don't use a server") for a budget
   with realistic data.
2. Settings → Experimental → toggle **Currency support** (sets the synced pref `flags.currency`).
3. Settings → Currency → pick **US Dollar**. Confirm a `$` now appears at each of the 7 areas:
   category autocomplete dropdown, close-account modal, desktop transaction table balance column +
   drag preview + split error, account balance history hover tooltip, mobile transaction row and
   running balance, mobile split editor footer and "Use remaining" button.
4. **The real test — switch to Japanese Yen (0 decimals).** Every migrated site must show `¥1,000`,
   not `¥10.00`. Before this change those sites show `10.00`. Compare against a site that already
   uses `useFormat` (any reports card, or the account balance header) to confirm they now agree.
5. Set Symbol Position to **After amount** and enable **Add space between amount and symbol**;
   confirm every migrated site follows, including the `<Trans>` ones.
6. Switch back to **None** and confirm output is identical to `master` — this is the no-regression
   check for the 99% of users who never enable the flag.

## PR

- Title must be prefixed `[AI]`, per
  [pr-and-commit-rules.md](.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md). Leave the PR template blank and
  unchecked.
- Release note required in `upcoming-release-notes/` (e.g. `currency-display-sites.md`). Recommend
  `category: Maintenance` since the flag is off by default and nothing user-visible ships; a
  maintainer may prefer `Bugfix` given it corrects wrong amounts for anyone who enabled the flag.
  Generate with `yarn generate:release-notes`.
- Worth stating in the description: this is step 1 of 3, the 0-decimal bug is the motivation, and
  site 13's markdown/bidi caveat.

  `debit`/`credit` cells — the edit path, untouched. They should pass unchanged.
- **VRT:** snapshots exist for `transactions`, `transactions.mobile`, `accounts`, `accounts.mobile`.
  With no currency selected, `getCurrency('')` gives `decimalPlaces: 2` and an empty symbol, so
  `format(x, 'financial')` is byte-identical to `integerToCurrency(x)` and
  [useFormat.ts:196](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts#L196) skips styling entirely.
  **Expect zero snapshot changes — if any snapshot moves, that's a real regression, not a rebaseline.**

Run:

```bash
yarn typecheck
yarn lint:fix
yarn workspace @actual-app/web run vitest --run TransactionsTable
yarn test
```

## Verification

The unit tests prove nothing about the actual fix, since they run at the default currency. Prove it
manually:

1. `yarn start`, then **View demo** on the setup screen (after "Don't use a server") for a budget
   with realistic data.
2. Settings → Experimental → toggle **Currency support** (sets the synced pref `flags.currency`).
3. Settings → Currency → pick **US Dollar**. Confirm a `$` now appears at each of the 7 areas:
   category autocomplete dropdown, close-account modal, desktop transaction table balance column +
   drag preview + split error, account balance history hover tooltip, mobile transaction row and
   running balance, mobile split editor footer and "Use remaining" button.
4. **The real test — switch to Japanese Yen (0 decimals).** Every migrated site must show `¥1,000`,
   not `¥10.00`. Before this change those sites show `10.00`. Compare against a site that already
   uses `useFormat` (any reports card, or the account balance header) to confirm they now agree.
5. Set Symbol Position to **After amount** and enable **Add space between amount and symbol**;
   confirm every migrated site follows, including the `<Trans>` ones.
6. Switch back to **None** and confirm output is identical to `master` — this is the no-regression
   check for the 99% of users who never enable the flag.

## PR

- Title must be prefixed `[AI]`, per
  [pr-and-commit-rules.md](.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md). Leave the PR template blank and
  unchecked.
- Release note required in `upcoming-release-notes/` (e.g. `currency-display-sites.md`). Recommend
  `category: Maintenance` since the flag is off by default and nothing user-visible ships; a
  maintainer may prefer `Bugfix` given it corrects wrong amounts for anyone who enabled the flag.
  Generate with `yarn generate:release-notes`.
- Worth stating in the description: this is step 1 of 3, the 0-decimal bug is the motivation, and
  site 13's markdown/bidi caveat.

```text
# AGENTS.md - Guide for AI Agents Working with Actual Budget

This guide provides comprehensive information for AI agents (like Cursor) working with the Actual Budget codebase.

## Project Overview

**Actual Budget** is a local-first personal finance tool written in TypeScript/JavaScript. It's 100% free and open-source with synchronization capabilities across devices.

- **Repository**: https://github.com/actualbudget/actual
- **Community Docs**: Documentation is part of the monorepo at `packages/docs/`. Published at https://actualbudget.org/docs
- **License**: MIT
- **Primary Language**: TypeScript (with React)
- **Build System**: Yarn 4 workspaces (monorepo)

## Quick Start Commands

### Essential Commands (Run from Root)

```bash
# Type checking (ALWAYS run before committing)
yarn typecheck

# Linting and formatting (with auto-fix)
yarn lint:fix

# Run all tests
yarn test

# Start development server (browser)
yarn start

# Start with sync server
yarn start:server-dev

# Start desktop app development
yarn start:desktop
```

### Important Rules

- **ALWAYS run yarn commands from the root directory** - never run them in child workspaces
- Use `yarn workspace <workspace-name> run <command>` for workspace-specific tasks
- Tests run once and exit by default (using `vitest --run`)

### ⚠️ PR titles must start with `[AI]`

Every pull request title must be prefixed with `[AI]` — you have to apply it
yourself. See [PR and Commit Rules](.github/agents/pr-and-commit-rules.md).

### Task Orchestration with Lage

The project uses **[lage](https://microsoft.github.io/lage/)** (a task runner for JavaScript monorepos) to efficiently run tests and other tasks across multiple workspaces:

- **Parallel execution**: Runs tests in parallel across workspaces for faster feedback
- **Smart caching**: Caches test results to skip unchanged packages (cached in `.lage/` directory)
- **Dependency awareness**: Understands workspace dependencies and execution order
- **Continues on error**: Uses `--continue` flag to run all packages even if one fails

**Lage Commands:**

```bash
# Run all tests across all packages
yarn test                    # Equivalent to: lage test --continue

# Run tests without cache (for debugging/CI)
yarn test:debug              # Equivalent to: lage test --no-cache --continue
```

Configuration is in `lage.config.js` at the project root.

## Architecture & Package Structure

### Core Packages

#### 1. **loot-core** (`packages/loot-core/`)

The core application logic that runs on any platform.

- Business logic, database operations, and calculations
- Platform-agnostic code
```

commit 93cce07542d44f3492342c29f083d8a1f2b2045a
Author: Stephen Brown II <Stephen.Brown2@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Jan 13 17:19:19 2026 -0500

    fix(privacy): hide currency symbols in redacted overlay (#6438)
    
    * fix(privacy): hide currency symbols in redacted overlay
    
    Add RedactedContent component that uses useLayoutEffect to walk the DOM
    and replace non-alphanumeric characters (like currency symbols) with spaces.
    This ensures characters not rendered by Redacted Script font are hidden,
    regardless of how deeply nested they are in the component tree.
    
    * refactor: simplify RedactedContent text node processing loop

diff --git a/packages/desktop-client/src/components/PrivacyFilter.tsx b/packages/desktop-client/src/components/PrivacyFilter.tsx
index 1053ce0ce..f2968e5eb 100644
--- a/packages/desktop-client/src/components/PrivacyFilter.tsx

@@ -1,8 +1,10 @@
 // @ts-strict-ignore

   Children,
   type ComponentPropsWithRef,

+  useLayoutEffect,

 } from 'react';
 
 import { useResponsive } from '@actual-app/components/hooks/useResponsive';
@@ -67,6 +69,36 @@ export function PrivacyFilter({
   );
 }
 
+type RedactedContentProps = {
+  children: ReactNode;
+};
+
+// Component that filters text content to remove non-alphanumeric characters
+// This works by intercepting the actual rendered text via a ref and modifying it
+function RedactedContent({ children }: RedactedContentProps) {
+  const containerRef = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
+
+  useLayoutEffect(() => {
+    if (containerRef.current) {
+      // Walk all text nodes and replace non-alphanumeric characters
+      const walker = document.createTreeWalker(
+        containerRef.current,
+        NodeFilter.SHOW_TEXT,
+        null,
+      );
+
+      let node: Text | null;
+      while ((node = walker.nextNode() as Text | null)) {
+        if (node.textContent) {
+          node.textContent = node.textContent.replace(/[^a-zA-Z0-9]/g, '*');
+        }
+      }
+    }

# Answers

## 1. Scope discipline — keep `FinancialText` out of this PR

**Argue: separate follow-up.** Evidence:

`FinancialText` (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/FinancialText.tsx:13-21`) is purely typographic — it renders `<Component {...props} style={{ ...style, ...styles.tnum }} />` with `Component` defaulting to `Text`, and `styles.tnum` is a single declaration (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/component-library/src/styles.ts:92-97`):

```
fontFeatureSettings: '"tnum", "ss01", "ss04"'
```

That has nothing to do with the decimal-places bug this PR fixes.

**Would it break VRT/tests?**

- **Sites 11–12: no, it's pixel-safe but zero-value.** Those spans already spread `styles.tnum` manually (`TransactionListItem.tsx:284,300`). `Text` is a bare `<span>` + emotion class (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/component-library/src/Text.tsx:15-23`), so `<FinancialText>` yields the *same* `<span>`, not a nested one. The only ordering difference is that `FinancialText` puts `tnum` **last** while the current code puts it first/middle — and the co-spread objects are `makeAmountFullStyle()` (returns `{ color }` only, `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/util.ts:119-126`) and `getTextStyle()` (`fontSize`/`fontStyle`/`color`, `TransactionListItem.tsx:50-63`). No `fontFeatureSettings` collision → identical computed CSS → identical pixels. Only the emotion hash changes, and nothing queries by class.
- **Sites 3 and 7: yes, this would churn snapshots.** Neither is tnum today. Site 3 sits inside `<Trans>`/`<strong>` prose and site 7 inside `<PrivacyFilter>`. Introducing tabular figures changes digit advance widths, which *will* shift `Accounts-closes-an-account-1..6-chromium-linux.png`. Pure cost, no correctness benefit.

**So:** the free change (11–12) is not worth widening the diff; the non-free change (3, 7) is actively harmful here. There are **34 manual `styles.tnum` spreads across 18 files** in `desktop-client` — this is its own mechanical, repo-wide cleanup PR, reviewable on its own terms with a single deliberate snapshot-update commit.

## 2. Site 13 — migrate it (one line), don't delete

**It really is dead.** The `amount` menu item is commented out at `TransactionList.tsx:563-567`, and `onSuccess` is defined inline for exactly one `onBatchEdit` call (`:486`), so `name === 'amount'` is unreachable.

**The corruption fear doesn't materialize.** `compileMessage` (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/Notifications.tsx:42,47`) uses:

```js
paragraph.split(/(\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\))/g)
part.match(/\[([^\]]*)\]\(([^)]*)\)/)
```

The label class is `[^\]]*` and the href class is `[^)]*`. U+202A / U+202C / U+202F are neither `]` nor `)`, so the link still parses. And the action lookup is `actions[href.slice(1)]` (`:52,59`) against the key `[String(displayValue)]` — both derive from the *same* string, so they stay in sync. No currency symbol in `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/loot-core/src/shared/currencies.ts` contains a bracket or paren.

**Why migrate rather than delete:** the swap is a runtime no-op today (dead branch), so regression risk is zero; it removes the file's last `integerToCurrency` reference so the import can go, which is the actual point of the PR; and if the menu item is ever uncommented, currency-correct is what you want. Deleting the branch is the tempting-but-wrong move — the commented-out menu item at `:563-567` documents deliberate intent ("Add support later on until we have more user friendly amount input modal"), and silently removing its handler would make re-enabling it produce a raw integer.

Two genuinely pre-existing problems worth a **separate** issue, not this PR: (a) the notification message at `:515` is an untranslated template literal; (b) using the display value as both link label and href fragment is fragile for *every* case — the `notes` branch at `:507` already interpolates arbitrary user text that can contain `]` or `)`.

## 3. Site 4 `hideFraction` — cannot diverge; not a behavior change

The `hideFraction` prop on `Transaction` has exactly one use in the whole file:

```ts
// TransactionsTable.tsx:1191
const amountStyle = hideFraction ? { letterSpacing: -0.5 } : null;
```

It is **letter-spacing only**. It never touched digit rendering. The digits came from `integerToCurrency`'s default `getNumberFormat().formatter`, i.e. the module-global `numberFormatConfig` (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/loot-core/src/shared/util.ts:295-301,320-328`), which `useFormat` keeps in sync via `setNumberFormat` (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormat.ts:136-138`). So before and after, digit count is driven by the same `useSyncedPref('hideFraction')` value.

The one place the prop is hardcoded, `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/reports/Calendar.tsx:668` (`hideFraction={false}`), therefore only opts out of the letter-spacing tweak — it never forced 2 decimals. Everywhere else the prop originates from the same pref: `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/accounts/Account.tsx:2022,2079`.

**Verdict: no divergence, no behavior change.** Worth a line in the PR description so a reviewer doesn't have to re-derive it.

## 4. Naming convention — confirmed by grep

- **`format`, unanimously.** `const format = useFormat()` → **91** occurrences. `const formatter = useFormat()` → **0**. Any other identifier → **0**.
- **date-fns aliasing: `format as formatDate`, 10 occurrences.** (`from '@actual-app/core/shared/months'` uses `monthUtilFormat` ×3 and `formatDate` ×1.) The landed `BalanceHistoryGraph.tsx:12` change follows this correctly. `formatAmount`/`fmt` have zero precedent — don't invent one.
- Import path: `import { useFormat } from '#hooks/useFormat';` — matches the `#hooks/*` block already present in all four remaining files.

## 5. Test impact — nothing breaks

**`TransactionsTable.test.tsx`** is the only unit test touching any of the 13 files (I grepped every `*.test.ts{,x}` under `desktop-client/src` for the other component names — no hits; the only mobile test is `MobilePayeesPage.test.tsx`).

Its three `integerToCurrency` references (`:15,523,531`) are the **expected-value helper**, and they assert on the `debit`/`credit` cells — which render via `amountToCurrency` (`TransactionsTable.tsx:1783,1786,1817`), **not** one of the 13 sites. Untouched.

Site 4's balance `<Cell>` is gated on `showBalance`, and `showBalances` is absent from `defaultProps` (`TransactionsTable.test.tsx:289-308`) → never rendered in tests.

**And even if it were, the strings are identical.** `TestProviders` (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/mocks.tsx:42-56`) uses a fresh store with empty synced prefs, so `useSyncedPref('defaultCurrencyCode')` is `undefined` → `getCurrency('')` → `currencies[0]` = `{ code: '', symbol: '', decimalPlaces: 2 }` (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/loot-core/src/shared/currencies.ts:23,72-74`). With `code === ''`, `useFormat.ts:196` skips `applyCurrencyStyling` entirely, and `decimalPlaces` is 2. So `format(x, 'financial') === integerToCurrency(x)` byte-for-byte under test.

**VRT:** snapshots exist for all affected surfaces — `Accounts-closes-an-account-*` (site 3), `Transactions-checks-the-page-visuals-*` (site 4), `Mobile-Accounts-opens-individual-account-page-*` (sites 11–12), `Mobile-Transactions-creates-a-transaction-via-footer-button-*` (sites 8–10). They all run with the flag **off** and no `defaultCurrencyCode` (no e2e test touches currency — only `budget.mobile.test.ts:4,84` imports `currencyToAmount`), so output is unchanged and **no snapshot should need regenerating**. If one does, that's a red flag, not a rebaseline. ## 6. Verification — how to actually prove it

**Fast path (recommended).** `yarn start`, open a budget, then in the browser console:

```js
await window.$send('preferences/save', { id: 'flags.currency',        value: 'true' });
await window.$send('preferences/save', { id: 'defaultCurrencyCode',   value: 'JPY'  });
location.reload();
```

`window.$send` is exposed at `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/index.tsx:81`. This mirrors exactly what `saveSyncedPrefs` does (`/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/prefs/prefsSlice.ts:125-128`) minus the `mergeSyncedPrefs` redux dispatch — hence the reload.

**UI path (equivalent, no console):** Settings → show advanced → Experimental → check "Currency support" (`settings/Experimental.tsx:199-204`) → a Currency block appears (`settings/index.tsx:240`) → pick "Japanese Yen". Also flip **symbol position = after** and **space between amount and symbol** (`useFormat.ts:153-159`) — those exercise the `\u202F` and `\u202A…\u202C` paths that plain `integerToCurrency` can never produce, so they're the sharpest tell that a site is on the new funnel.

**Why JPY is the right probe:** `JPY` has `decimalPlaces: 0` (`currencies.ts:46`; same for `KRW` and `IRR`). An amount stored as integer `1000` renders `1,000.00` through the old path (hardcoded `decimalPlaces = 2` at `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/loot-core/src/shared/util.ts:447-456`) and `‪¥‬1,000` through `useFormat`. That's a **wrong number**, not a missing glyph — easy to eyeball.

**Per-site click path:**

| Site | How to reach it |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | Any category autocomplete with balances shown (transaction category cell) |
| 3 | Account → Close Account, on an account with nonzero balance |
| 4 | Account page → enable "Show running balance" → Balance column |
| 5 | Drag a transaction row (drag preview) |
| 6 | Create a split whose children don't sum to the parent → "Amount left:" popover |
| 7 | Sidebar: hover an account name → hover the sparkline |
| 8–9 | Narrow viewport → open a transaction → split it → footer button |
| 10 | Same, then focus a split amount field → "Use remaining:" |
| 11–12 | Mobile account page transaction list; for 12 toggle the `show-balances-<accountId>` pref (`mobile/accounts/AccountPage.tsx:142`) |
| 13 | Dead — verify by inspection, or temporarily uncomment `TransactionList.tsx:563-567` |

**Regression sweep:** flip `defaultCurrencyCode` back to `None` and confirm every site returns to the plain 2-decimal string. Then `yarn typecheck && yarn lint && yarn test`.

## 7. PR shape and release note

**One PR.** It's ~7 files, one mechanical transform, one reviewable claim ("these were the last display-path `integerToCurrency` calls"). Splitting desktop/mobile would leave the tree in a half-migrated state with no independent value, and a reviewer can't verify "these are the last 13" from a partial diff. The commit precedent is exactly this shape: `9a9de5ee0` (budget), `37247395e` (schedules), `99ca34458` (rules) each did one surface-area sweep in one PR.

Do make the PR body state the two scope exclusions explicitly, since a reviewer's first instinct will be "you missed some":
- `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/util.ts:81` — `currencyToAmount(integerToCurrency(val))`, a round-trip that feeds a parser, not a display.
- `/Users/james/actual-budget/packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/envelope/CoverMenu.tsx:56` — seeds `useState` for a text input later read by `evalArithmetic` (`:60`).

**Yes, add a release note.** Behind-a-flag currency work has consistently shipped with one:

```
upcoming-release-notes/5907.md → category: Features / "Adds currency display to the schedules"
upcoming-release-notes/5908.md → category: Features / "Adds currency display to the budget"
upcoming-release-notes/5639.md → category: Features / "Adds currency display to the rules"
```

Valid categories per `/Users/james/actual-budget/bin/release-note-generator.mts:44-47` are `Features` / `Enhancements` / `Bugfixes` / `Maintenance` (note: the script says **`Bugfixes`**, while `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md:134` says `Bugfix` — the script wins).

I'd use **`Features`** to match the sibling PRs, phrased as a command per `index.md:139`, e.g. *"Add currency display to transaction tables, lists and modals"*. `Maintenance` would be defensible on "internal refactor" grounds but is wrong: for JPY/KRW/IRR users this fixes a visibly wrong number, which is user-facing. Run `yarn generate:release-notes` rather than hand-writing the file. Per the repo's AI rules, the PR title and every commit message need the `[AI]` prefix.

# Writing Release Notes for actualbudget/actual

Release notes are the user-facing changelog. Each code change adds one Markdown file to `upcoming-release-notes/`, and these get collected into the published changelog at the next release. The authoritative source is the **Writing Good Release Notes** section of `packages/docs/docs/contributing/index.md`. Read it if anything below is unclear.

## The file

Create `upcoming-release-notes/<slug>.md`, where `<slug>` is a **short, descriptive kebab-case slug** naming the change (e.g. `add-payee-autocomplete.md`, `fix-mobile-category-delete.md`). Do **not** use a PR number, since the PR link is resolved automatically at release time. (Numeric filenames like `1234.md` still work, but a slug is preferred.)

```markdown
---
category: Features
authors: [YourGitHubUsername]
---

Add payee autocomplete to the transaction entry form
```

- **`category`**: exactly one of `Features` (new feature), `Enhancements` (improvement to an existing feature), `Bugfix` (bug fix), or `Maintenance` (internal change with no user-visible effect).
- **`authors`**: array of the GitHub username(s) who did the work.

## Writing the entry

The body is the changelog line. It is read by everyday users, not developers.

- **One sentence.** Short and clear. No paragraphs, no bullet lists, no long prose.
- **Plain language, no technical detail.** Describe what changed for the user, not how it was built. Avoid file names, function names, internal component names, and implementation jargon. (Exception: `Maintenance` entries may be technical, since they are for internal changes.)
- **Phrase it as a command.** Start with a present-tense verb: "Add …", "Fix …", "Show …", not "Added …" or "Adds …".
- Generally match the PR title, but reword it if that reads more clearly to a user.

Good: `Fix incorrect balance when reconciling an account with future transactions`
Too technical: `Fix off-by-one in reconcileTransactions() when txn.date > today`


ARGUMENTS: Add a release note for migrating 13 currency display sites from integerToCurrency to the useFormat hook, so amounts render with the configured currency symbol and correct decimal places (fixes wrong amounts for 0-decimal currencies like JPY/KRW/IRR). Behind the experimental currency feature flag.

```text
# Getting Started (for Students)

This is a short guide to running **Actual Budget** on your own computer so you
can explore and experiment with it. Everything runs locally in your browser.

> Already comfortable with Node projects? The whole thing is:
> `git clone … && cd actual && yarn install && yarn start`, then open
> <http://localhost:3001> and click **View demo**.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

Install these once before you start:

| Tool | Version | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) | **22 or newer** | Check with `node -v` |
| [Yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/) | **4.9.1+** | Comes with Node via Corepack — see below |
| [Git](https://git-scm.com/) | any recent | On **Windows**, install "Git for Windows" — it also provides the `sh` and `bash` shells some scripts use |

> 💡 **New to Yarn workspaces?** Actual Budget uses [Yarn workspaces](https://yarnpkg.com/features/workspaces) to manage multiple packages in a single repo. You mostly run commands from the root — but understanding workspaces helps when something goes wrong in a sub-package.

> 📖 **Architecture overview:** Before diving in, read the [Contributing guide](https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/) — it walks through how the codebase is organized and how the sync server, web app, and shared packages relate to each other.

Enable the correct Yarn version (only needed once):

```bash
corepack enable
```

Yarn will then automatically use the version this project expects.

---

## 2. Install dependencies

Clone the project and install everything. `yarn install` downloads all the
dependencies into a local `node_modules` folder (which is **not** stored in Git —
that's why you install it yourself).
```
</details></tool-use>

_**Agent (claude-opus-5 2026-09-15 14:02:08-0400)**_

The next step is PR 2 (the edit/serialization paths), and the good news is its one design blocker is already solved in the codebase. The bad news is I under-sized it.

## The blocker is resolved

I'd flagged "non-hook modules can't call `useFormat`" as needing either a new global or threading the `format` function. Neither is necessary — there's already an established pattern. About a dozen files in [budget/goals/editor/](packages/desktop-client/src/components/budget/goals/editor/) thread `format.currency.decimalPlaces` as a plain number:

```ts
amountToInteger(template.amount, format.currency.decimalPlaces)
```

`useFormat()` exposes `.currency`, so any component that has the hook can pass the number (or code) down into a plain module function. And [`integerToCurrencyWithDecimal`](packages/loot-core/src/shared/util.ts#L458-L461) already accepts an optional `currencyCode`. So PR 2 is parameter-threading against existing precedent — no global, no architecture change.

## But the scope is roughly double what I told you

My earlier survey grepped `integerToCurrency` and `amountToCurrency`. That missed a whole class: **`integerToAmount` / `amountToInteger` with the default `decimalPlaces = 2`**, which has the same 0-decimal bug. Sites still hardcoded include [EnvelopeBudgetMenuModal.tsx:72,119](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/EnvelopeBudgetMenuModal.tsx#L72), [TrackingBudgetMenuModal.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/TrackingBudgetMenuModal.tsx#L72), [SplitAmountInput.tsx:88,94](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/SplitAmountInput.tsx#L88), [TransactionEdit.tsx:128,169,1317,1789](packages/desktop-client/src/components/mobile/transactions/TransactionEdit.tsx#L128), [ImportTransactionsModal.tsx](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/ImportTransactionsModal/ImportTransactionsModal.tsx#L365), [EditFieldModal.tsx:75](packages/desktop-client/src/components/modals/EditFieldModal.tsx#L75), [queries/index.ts:111](packages/desktop-client/src/queries/index.ts#L111), and [budget-analysis-export.ts:30-33](packages/desktop-client/src/components/reports/spreadsheets/budget-analysis-export.ts#L30).

So PR 2 is ~15 files, not the ~6 I implied.

## The constraint that makes it risky

These are **paired round-trips**. [table/utils.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/components/transactions/table/utils.ts) serializes with `integerToCurrencyWithDecimal` (line 64) and deserializes with `amountToInteger` (line 84) — both defaulting to 2. Today that's self-consistent: a JPY amount stored as `1000` becomes `"10.00"`, parses to `10`, and multiplies back to `1000`. The integer survives; only the number shown in the input is wrong.

**Change one side without the other and you corrupt stored amounts.** That's the difference between PR 2 and PR 1 — PR 1 was display-only and couldn't lose data. So PR 2 needs its sites classified into round-trip pairs and migrated pair-by-pair.

One judgment call I'd flag rather than decide alone: [useFormulaExecution.ts](packages/desktop-client/src/hooks/useFormulaExecution.ts#L244) passes a literal `2` in about six places. That may be intentional formula semantics rather than an oversight, and it's worth confirming with whoever owns formula mode before touching it.

## What I'd do

Audit and classify the edit sites into round-trip pairs first — a read-only pass producing the pair list — then migrate pair-by-pair against the `format.currency.decimalPlaces` precedent. That audit is what makes PR 2 safe, and it's cheap.

Two things still outstanding from PR 1: the release note still has the `REPLACE_WITH_GITHUB_USERNAME` placeholder, and nothing is committed yet — the 7 files and the note are sitting in the working tree on branch `currency`.

Want me to start the PR 2 audit, or close out PR 1 first (username + commit + PR)?
